column1: # Track T auto-pin baseline allowlist        <job selector>  <ticket slug>
# Reds listed here do NOT block an automatic pin. Everything else does.
# EVERY entry must name a ticket. An entry without one is refused at load and
# printed as ignored — that rule is the whole design. The allowlist is how "we
# are shipping with these known breaks" becomes an explicit, reviewable
# statement instead of a quiet dumping ground, and it only works if adding a
# line costs you a ticket.
# Two things can never be waived here:
#   * self-host byte-identical — a compiler that cannot reproduce itself must
#     never become the ground other tracks build on, allowlisted or not;
#   * a red that is not in this file — that is the point.
# Curated by humans and by Track T's face-2 agent. The daemon only ever READS
# it. Authority: decide-track-t-autopin-criteria (option A, reopened and chosen
# 2026-08-08 after the baseline cleared from 18 permanent reds to 2 of 2182).
# STATUS: ARMED since 2026-09-09 (`fc2ce3d02`; the switch is the committed file
# tstate/pin-armed). A `would_pin` now RUNS `make pin` — it no longer only logs to
# tstate/pin-shadow.log. So an entry here is LIVE: it decides whether a red stops
# the fleet's ground from moving.
# The paragraph this replaces said "shadow mode. Nothing moves `pinned` yet", and
# it was true when written. Left in place it tells a reader that adding a line is
# inert — the most expensive kind of stale row, because a reader who believes it
# does nothing and so generates nothing that could reveal the error. What retires
# THIS line in turn: tstate/pin-armed ceasing to exist.
# Empty is still correct as of 2026-09-10, and that is evidence rather than
# paperwork — the automation has never needed a waiver. The original note said a
# file still empty when shadow mode ended would be "the strongest possible
# argument the automation is safe"; shadow mode ended with it empty, so that
# argument was earned. The first entry spends some of it.
# So do not add a line to get past an inconvenient red. The one deadlock it
# legitimately resolves: a red that is NEW is by definition unbaselined, so
# `unexpected` is non-empty, so no pin fires, so `pinned` never moves, so the
# baseline never re-seeds — `seed_baseline` runs only on a pin CHANGE
# (twatch.py, pin_shadow: `if pin_id and base.get("pin") != pin_id`). Without a
# waiver that state cannot clear itself. With one, the job still runs and still
# goes red in every report; only its power to freeze pinning is suspended, and
# the ticket it names is what unsuspends it.
# Example of the required shape (commented out — not an active entry):
# test-zlib#00
# Added on the owner's answer, enrolling the six real-program jobs that were in
# no tier at all (bug-t-six-real-program-jobs-are-in-no-tier-so-they-never-run).
# Four of the six measure GREEN; these two do not, and the choice he made was
# visible-but-not-blocking over held-back-until-fixed -- a red that runs and
# reports is worth more than a job nobody can see.
# Both are ONE missing C declaration, both are statements about our tree rather
# than about any host, and neither is "add the declaration":
#   * __builtin_inf travels with a family (__builtin_inff/infl/nan/nans/
#     huge_val*). Declaring only the one duktape names greens this job and stops
#     the next corpus at the same wall.
#   * malloc_usable_size is worse. quickjs uses it for memory ACCOUNTING, so a
#     stub returning the requested size compiles, links, runs, and silently
#     under-reports whenever the allocator rounds up -- surfacing much later as
#     an engine memory limit behaving oddly under load, arbitrarily far from the
#     stub. No output comparison can catch that, the way none catches a leak.
# Selectors verified against testmgr.generate() rather than guessed: both
# targets decompose to exactly one job, `<target>#00`. The loader matches by
# exact dict membership with no globbing, so a misspelled selector would be a
# line that waives nothing and says nothing -- and both jobs classify as
# testmgr's `selfhost` CLASS, which is a scheduling bucket and is NOT what the
# unwaivable self-host check reads (that keys on the `selfhost-fixedpoint`
# name prefix). Checked, because a guard that cannot fire prints PASS.
# These leave the file the moment their tickets close.
test-duktape#00
test-quickjs#00
